steps.text: Preheat the oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C). Butter a 2-quart casserole dish.

In a large saucepan, sauté chopped onion in butter. Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute. Add chicken broth and milk. Heat to boiling, stirring constantly. Reduce heat to medium and cook and stir for 2 minutes more. Season with salt and pepper. Add frozen peas and carrots and cooked chicken. Pour mixture into the prepared casserole dish.

In a medium bowl, mix together 2 cups flour, baking powder, and 3/4 teaspoon salt. Cut in shortening until mixture is crumbly. Stir in milk just until dough is moistened, then drop by spoonfuls onto chicken mixture.

Bake at 450 degrees F (230 degrees C) for 12 to 15 minutes, or until biscuits are golden brown, and cooked on bottom. This tends to bubble over so I place a piece of aluminum foil under the pan to catch drips.

raw_recipe.headline: Chicken Biscuit Pie
raw_recipe.description: This easy homemade pot pie combines cooked chicken, peas, carrots, and onion in a creamy chicken sauce. Top with spoonfuls of drop biscuit dough, or use premade refrigerated biscuits.
raw_recipe.name: Chicken Biscuit Pie

review.reviewBody: I gave this recipe 4 stars but with a few changes it is a 5. I am the kitchen manager for a rescue mission and have to feed alot of people on a small budget. And this dish is definetly a low cost meal that delivers big results. Here are the changes I made - first I sauteed together chopped onions, celery & carrots - which is called a mirepoix. Then I added the flour and then milk with some chicken stock. To this I added additional seasoning - garlic powder, thyme, rosemary, and sage. Then I added canned vegetables and canned chicken. Of course fresh would be better - but I use what comes in the back door - so we get alot of canned items. The consistency is like thick gravy. Then I poured this mixture into my pans. I have a bakery mix that is much like Bisquick I used to make the biscuit mixture. In reading the other reviews I noticed that the same issue kept coming up - the biscuits were done on top but still gooey/runny on the bottom. So I made my biscuit mixture a little on the "sloppy" side - not runny like pancake batter - and not doughy like biscuit dough - but somewhere in the middle- "gloppy". Then I spooned the biscuit batter on top of the chicken mixture in spoonfuls that left about a inch space around the "glop" as the glop will rise and expand as it cooks. It is important to leave a little room around your glops as this allows the biscuits to cook through. I got sloppy with my glops on the last pan and put them too close together and they didn't cook all the way th

I preheated the oven at 450 degrees first, prepared the biscuit dough before I made the chicken mixture. I used fresh buttermilk and cold butter for the biscuit dough. I used half butter instead of all butter, low-sodium chicken broth and half-n-half milk for the chicken mixture. I use frozen peas with pearl onions, added diced celery, 1 medium orange, yellow and purple sweet carrots diced. For seasoning I added 1tsp of poultry seasoning, 1 garlic clove, chopped, fresh rosemary, fresh ground black pepper and Hawaiian sea salt. As soon as I made the biscuit dough I quickly spooned them on top the HOT chicken mixture to start cooking the biscuits immediately. This helps avoid any soggy biscuits on the bottom. I had 12 biscuits spaced about 1 inch apart. I used a 13x9 dish and covered the dish with aluminum foil. I baked the chicken at 375 degrees for 30 minutes, turned off the oven, uncover the foil from pan, brushed the tops of biscuits with melted butter for a golden crust and left the mixture for 10 minutes before removing. The gravy was thick, creamy and savory! The chicken was tender and vegetables cooked just right. The biscuits were not soggy but golden brown, flaky and delicious. They rose and expanded while baking up almost touching each other. I served this chicken biscuit pie over a small mound of, “Creamy Smashed Potatoes,” also from this website. This is a true comfort food-very hearty, tasty and fulfilling.

This was great for a cold, wintry evening. As other reviewers suggested, I prepared the biscuit dough first so that I could put it on the hot filling right away. My brother and I are not fans of peas, so I used frozen carrots and green beans. I preheated the oven to 425 degrees, then baked it in a 13 x 9 pan at 375 degrees for 30 minutes—the biscuits were baked perfectly. We all agreed that there wasn’t enough of the filling, so next time I’d make 1.5 times the amount.

This was so delish. We made two separate dishes one with gluten-free biscuits and one with regular biscuits. I used gluten-free flour to thicken the filling and lactose-free milk because we all do better without the extra dairy. I didn't have peas so I used frozen green beans. I followed others' suggestions and added garlic powder and I increased the broth to 2.5 cups to thin it out and make more sauce. My kids loved it and one of them ate the leftovers for breakfast.

Great idea for using leftover roast chicken! I also sautéed onion with diced carrot and celery (mirepoix) and added additional herbs - 1 teaspoon each of garlic powder, sage, rosemary and thyme as well as a bay leaf. Without those spices, the sauce would have been quite bland. Also, I added an additional cup of liquid (part broth, part milk) and 3 chopped russet potatoes. This increased the cooking time on the stove by 20 minutes. Agree that the biscuits were a bit tough so I will look for another recipe the next time I make this dish.

Love this recipe! Very quick. Using a large silver pan, doubled the recipe, but added a few dashes of garlic salt, a few more dashes of pepper an extra 1/2 cup of broth. Also, instead of making the biscuit dough, used two cans of Grands biscuits (8 in each; use plain, not butter flavor). The Grands calls for a 350 degree oven and the recipe calls for a 450 degree oven so I just placed a piece of foil on top of the biscuits after 10 minutes (did not tighten) because they browned too fast. I turned the oven off to let the dish sit for about 20 minutes in the heat. Next time I will bake using the instructions on the biscuit can. This is recipe is indeed a keeper! Will probably use Grands Jr. biscuits or regular sized biscuits next time (two cans of smaller sized biscuits for doubling the recipe should be perfect and without too much bread).

Great recipe! I changed a couple of things. I bought frozen mixed vegetables and simmered them in chicken broth. It have them a great texture and cooked them a little before adding them to the mixture. I also breaded and pan fried chicken breasts and cut them into cubes. I made my own biscuits using my own recipe. I cooked mine a little longer and kept an eye on keeping the temperature a little lower ( around 350) this kept the biscuits from burning on top. I liked the other viewers suggestion to put biscuits on top while the mixture is hot so it will start cooking. The

I used the basic ideas here, but did change the recipe quite a bit. I doubled the recipe for two families, used more chicken, frozen mixed vegetables, and canned biscuits to make it all faster and easier. The biscuits, I pulled in half horizontally, and they seemed to bake through quite well. I baked the dish at 350 for about 40 minutes. I used large enough casserole dishes that the mixture didn't bubble over in the oven, which is always a good thing. It turned out really good and a satisfying comfort food.

This was so good and perfect for a cold Winter day. I added some chopped celery and fresh chopped carrots along with the onions. I also added some sage which gave it a great flavor. I'm a vegetarian so I used vegetable broth and vegetarian chicken pieces. I baked it at 400 degrees for about 20 minutes. I did find the biscuit topping to be a little undercooked like other reviewers, but it was still very good. Thanks for the great recipe!

This was great! Will do again. I'll probably place the biscuits lightly on top rather than smash them down into the mixture. I added 1/2 cup more of chicken broth to get more "gravy". Also added corn to the mix...love the veggies.

I've made this recipe many times over the years, and my family loves it!! I always add more vegetables, such as small cut broccoli florets and red bell peppers, and because of this, I double the cream sauce amount. Then I add frozen buttermilk biscuits to the top instead of dropping my own and just follow the bake time on the biscuits package.

The food on my plate did NOT look like the pretty picture, but the biscuit was tasty and the chicken mixture was excellent, too. The directions for the biscuits included every measurement but the one for baking powder. It would also have helped if "milk" were included in the ingredient list for the chicken mixture AND the biscuits. When I saw "stir in milk," I panicked; I thought I had mistakenly added milk to the chicken mixture.

Yummmm. You could change this around and make it anyway you want. I used the freezer biscuits you buy in a bag. I cooked them according to the biscuits directions. They weren't all the way done on the bottom, so I would lower the heat or put on a lid or stick it in the microwave.

I used a bag of frozen mixed peas and carrots and frozen biscuits, thawed. Increased the sauce and used more chicken than 2 cups. Baked in a 9x13 pan for at least 30 minutes to make sure biscuits were done. It was awesome.
Love this quick and easy way to make pot pie. I do use ready to bake Biscuits so is easier to make on a busy night.

I love this recipe but I cheat on the ingredients, sometimes using peas and carrots and sometimes using broccoli instead. Also I use big fluffy canned biscuits instead of making my own. To make it heart healthy I substitute sun flower oil or other seed oil for butter.

I added garlic and Vegeta because I add those things to almost everything I cook. I made the sauce base on the stovetop in a 14" stainless steel pan that I could transfer right into the oven, with no overflow. I dropped the biscuits in many little dollops rather than a few large biscuit-sized drops and they cooked through in 15 minutes. This is a very comforting dish that seems highly adaptable to personal tastes, and I will definitely make it again.
tasty & easy option to using up leftover cooked chicken

Very tasty! I omitted onion, & added red potato, leftover sweet potato, along with carrots, corn, peas & green beans. I used Cresent rolls because it was available. Very tasty. I usually make pie crust but may do the rolls next time.
